:::caution
This rule is part of the [nursery](/linter/#nursery) group. This means that it is experimental and the behavior can change at any time.
:::
## Summary
- Rule available since: `v2.6.5`
- Diagnostic Category: [`lint/nursery/noVueThisInTemplate`](/reference/diagnostics#diagnostic-category)
- This rule has an [**unsafe**](/linter/#unsafe-fixes) fix.
- The default severity of this rule is [**information**](/reference/diagnostics#information).
- This rule belongs to the following domains:
  - [`vue`](/linter/domains#vue)
- Sources: 
  - Inspired from [`vue/this-in-template`](https://eslint.vuejs.org/rules/this-in-template)

## How to configure
```json title="biome.json"
{
	"linter": {
		"rules": {
			"nursery": {
				"noVueThisInTemplate": "error"
			}
		}
	}
}

```
## Description
Disallow `this` in Vue templates.

Vue templates can read the properties of the component directly. Writing `this.count`
in a template does the same thing as writing `count`, so `this` only adds noise.

The rule doesn't report `this.name` when writing `name` alone would mean something else,
for example when a `v-for` or `v-slot` variable, or a function parameter, has the same name.

:::note
This rule reads Vue templates, which requires
[`html.experimentalFullSupportEnabled`](https://biomejs.dev/reference/configuration/#htmlexperimentalfullsupportenabled)
to be `true`. Without that setting, the rule reports nothing.
:::

## Examples

### Invalid

```vue
<template>
  <a :href="this.url">{{ text }}</a>
</template>
```

<Fragment set:html={"<pre class=\"language-text\"><code class=\"language-text\"></code></pre>"} />

```vue
<template>
  <p>{{ this.text }}</p>
</template>
```

<Fragment set:html={"<pre class=\"language-text\"><code class=\"language-text\"></code></pre>"} />

```vue
<template>
  <button @click="this.count++">Add</button>
</template>
```

<Fragment set:html={"<pre class=\"language-text\"><code class=\"language-text\"></code></pre>"} />

### Valid

```vue
<template>
  <a :href="url">{{ text }}</a>
  <button @click="count++">Add</button>
  <!-- `item` alone would be the `v-for` variable. -->
  <p v-for="item in items">{{ this.item }}</p>
</template>
```
